era_note: Connellsville, Fayette County, Pennsylvania, 2001-2016. R3: a real unsolved killing and living people. Per episode_spec: no depiction of the killing, the victim, autopsy or mortuary imagery, the mark on the hand, dental casts, or any likeness of the real people. No Short may name or imply who killed Curtis Haith, and no Short may assert in narration that bite-mark analysis is junk science - the film only reports that the expert who gave the evidence described it that way, and no Short repeats even that.

shorts.angle: A question was asked, and the answer moved. The expert revised the timing of the mark to a three-minute window without looking at anything new.
shorts.avoids: No image or description of the mark itself, the hand, the autopsy, or dental casts. No claim that the method is junk science. No claim about who killed anybody. The line stops at what the record says the expert did, not at what he intended.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: Nothing new was found and nothing new was tested. So what made the answer change?
shorts.loop_join: The last line returns to the problem the first line opened on: the question that had no answer.

lines.text: A problem surfaced with the comparison, and it was a serious one. A mark on a hand could have been left hours before a man died.
source_lines: A problem surfaced with the bite mark, and it was a serious one.
A bite on a hand could have been left hours before a man died. It could have been left days before. If it was days before, it proved nothing about the night of the murder at all.

lines.text: It could have been left days before. If it was days before, it proved nothing about the night of the murder at all.

lines.text: So the question of timing was put back to the investigation. Officers were directed to look into it, and the expert was asked to update his opinion.

lines.text: He did. He determined it had happened seven to ten minutes before the death.
source_lines: He did.
He determined that the bite had occurred seven to ten minutes before Curtis Haith's death.

shorts.angle: The first statement against her carried a detail the laboratory had disproved twenty months earlier. It was checkable in an afternoon, and the case went on.
shorts.avoids: Does not name the witness and does not say or imply that he, or anyone else, killed Curtis Haith. Does not depict the killing, the victim, or the scene. Reports only that the detail was wrong, which the record establishes.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: The one checkable detail was already ruled out. Why did that not stop it?
shorts.loop_join: The last line hands the case a direction, which is where the first line's twenty months of nothing ends.

lines.text: Twenty months went by like that. Then, in October of two thousand and two, a man who had dated her before went to the police.
source_lines: Twenty months went by like that.
In October of two thousand and two, a man named Thomas Beal went to the police.
Weimer had dated Beal before she was seeing Gibson. What he told officers was that Weimer and Gibson had killed Curtis Haith.

lines.text: According to him, she had told him something specific. She had told him that the blood on her clothes was the dead man's.
source_lines: According to Beal, Weimer had told him something specific. She had told him that the blood on her clothes was Haith's.

lines.text: The laboratory had established, twenty months earlier, that the blood on her clothes was her boyfriend's. Exactly as she had said.
source_lines: The DNA had already established, twenty months earlier, that the blood on her clothes was Gibson's.
The blood on Crystal Weimer's clothes was Michael Gibson's blood. Exactly as she had said.

lines.text: So the first statement against her contained a fact that the evidence had already ruled out.
source_lines: So the first statement against her contained a fact that the evidence had already ruled out.

lines.text: There is a straightforward test available at that moment, and it costs nothing. The statement contains a checkable detail. Check it.
source_lines: There is a straightforward test available at that moment, and it costs nothing. A witness reports a confession. The confession contains a checkable detail. Check it.

lines.text: If the detail is wrong, the witness either misremembered, or was told wrong, or is making it up. You find out which before you build on him.
source_lines: If the detail is wrong, the witness either misremembered, or was told wrong, or is making it up — and you find out which before you build on him.

lines.text: The detail was wrong. He was not set aside, and the investigation now had a direction.
source_lines: The detail was wrong. Beal was not set aside. The investigation now had a direction, and the direction was a woman whose physical evidence had cleared her twenty months earlier.

lines.text: The direction was a woman whose physical evidence had cleared her. It points away from her. It does not point at her once.
source_lines: The detail was wrong. Beal was not set aside. The investigation now had a direction, and the direction was a woman whose physical evidence had cleared her twenty months earlier.

shorts.angle: The witness took it back under oath and the charges were dismissed. She was home for six months. Then a man in prison offered to implicate her for a lighter sentence, and she was arrested again.
shorts.avoids: Does not name the witness or the prisoner, and does not say or imply that either of them killed anybody. Does not depict the killing, the victim, or any real person. Does not characterise the prosecutor's intent; the record establishes the sequence, not the motive.
shorts.funnel_question_left_for_longform: A witness took it back on the stand and a judge sent her home. What brought her back?
shorts.loop_join: The last line returns to the courtroom of the first, with the case standing exactly where the witness had left it.

lines.text: A preliminary hearing is not a trial. It is a low bar, deliberately: the Commonwealth has only to show there is enough to believe this defendant did it.
source_lines: A preliminary hearing is not a trial. It is a low bar, deliberately: the Commonwealth has only to show that a crime happened and that there is enough to believe this defendant did it. Cases are not supposed to end there.

lines.text: At that hearing the Commonwealth called its witness to the stand as a witness of fact. Under oath, he took it all back.
source_lines: At that hearing, the Commonwealth called Thomas Beal to the stand as a witness of fact.
Under oath, Beal took it all back.

lines.text: He testified that an officer had, in his words, kind of like coaxed him along on how to do it.
source_lines: He testified that an officer had — his words — "kind of like coaxed me along on how to do it."

lines.text: The judge dismissed the charges. Crystal Weimer went home. She was home for six months.
source_lines: The judge dismissed the charges. Crystal Weimer went home.
She was home for six months.

lines.text: Then, in July of two thousand and four, a man in prison made an offer. He would implicate her in the murder.
source_lines: In July of two thousand and four, Joseph Stenger made an offer.
He told police he would implicate Weimer in the murder. In exchange, he wanted a lighter sentence on convictions of his own, in an unrelated matter.

lines.text: In exchange, he wanted a lighter sentence on convictions of his own, in an unrelated matter. This time it went to trial.

lines.text: On the strength of that statement, officers arrested her a second time and charged her again.
source_lines: On the strength of that statement, officers arrested Crystal Weimer for a second time and charged her again.

lines.text: Nevertheless, investigators continued to focus their efforts on her. Nothing new had been found. Nothing new had been tested.
